title: Legacy FoxPro program recreated
text: Reverse-engineers a legacy FoxPro program by running it in a DOS emulator, stepping through every screen and inspecting its data files, then recreates it near-identically in one week.

title: Wi-Fi camera neural accelerator
text: Reverse-engineers the neural network accelerator inside a cheap Wi-Fi camera chip, then writes a compiler and runtime so the camera runs custom networks.

title: AAC support for Linux video editor
text: Reverse-engineers the Linux build of a video editor to add missing AAC audio decoding, patching it to route streams through ffmpeg.

title: Amplifier protocol and iOS app
text: Reverse-engineers the proprietary control protocol of networked amplifiers, then builds an iOS controller app to replace the manufacturer's abandoned official app.

title: 800K-line chemistry code distilled
text: Reverse-engineers an 800,000-line Python and C chemistry codebase from a closed startup, extracts its core ideas, and rewrites an equivalent in 10,000 lines on modern GPU frameworks.

title: Security camera traffic decoded
text: Sniffs network traffic between camera recorders and cameras, decodes the WebSocket streams, and builds a proxy that dewarps 360-degree video with a native Apple GPU shader pipeline.

title: Lab instrument raw data format
text: Decompiles a lab instrument's vendor executable to recover its raw data format, then builds an analysis suite for files the instrument otherwise exports only as PDF reports.

title: 1997 PC game decompiled
text: Decompiles a 1997 PC game, sets up a reverse-engineering environment, and shims its DirectX library to run it headlessly on modern hardware.

title: Gadgets probed over USB
text: Reverse-engineers consumer electronics over USB to dump a mixer's full state for software control, revive old remotes, and write a replacement printer driver for a new operating system.

title: Hardware device wire protocol
text: Reverse-engineers the wire protocol of an expensive hardware device from very little data, keeping a plan file and a facts-only knowledge base of every discovery.

title: Firmware pulled from vendor installer
text: Extracts firmware from a vendor update installer and analyzes it with Ghidra and radare2 to find a plausible cause of a reported problem, documenting each step.

title: Undocumented IDE plugin protocol
text: Reverse-engineers an undocumented editor integration protocol from the WebSocket traffic of the official plugins to build a compatible client.

title: Neural Engine training gradients
text: Gets LoRA fine-tuning gradients running on a laptop chip's neural engine, which has no public training API, by iterating on real hardware to find its undocumented limits.

title: Figma binary protocol
text: Reverse-engineers a design tool's binary WebSocket protocol so a script can read and write live files, bypassing the REST interface and its rate limits.

title: Printer scanning protocol and driver
text: Reverse-engineers a printer maker's network scanning protocol from packet captures and writes an open-source macOS print and scan driver in Rust.

title: FPGA bitstream format
text: Reverse-engineers the proprietary bitstream format of a Cyclone IV FPGA so open-source synthesis and place-and-route tools can target the chip.

title: CAD 3D format to STEP
text: Reverse-engineers a CAD application's 3D solid format to convert DWG drawings to the STEP exchange format.

title: Tower-building game decompiled
text: Decompiles a 1990s tower-building game in Ghidra and rewrites it in WebAssembly, parsing the original assets from a copy the player supplies.

title: Life-sim game memory exposed
text: Reverse-engineers a life-simulation game with a Ghidra bridge to expose household money and character needs through a tool server.

title: Automated firmware reverse engineering
text: Drives radare2 and Ghidra automatically to analyze firmware and reimplement it, recovering pinouts and peripheral bring-up so old hardware runs on modern toolchains.

title: Keyboard battery level on macOS
text: Reads a Bluetooth keyboard's HID descriptor off a live connection, finds no battery field, and adds firmware and a menu-bar app that report charge on macOS.

title: Apple Notes export
text: Reverse-engineers a notes app's storage to export thousands of notes with folders, formatting, images and voice recordings in seconds.

title: Deminify a Bun CLI
text: Decompiles a bundled Bun command-line app and renames each minified function and variable with suggested names applied deterministically, to read its implementation.

title: Hidden usage-limit headers
text: Captures rate-limit headers from API responses through a local proxy to work out the undisclosed formula behind a service's usage limits.

title: Reconstructing a CLI's source
text: Points a coding assistant at a command-line tool's own installation directory and has seven parallel workers piece together as much of its source code as possible.

title: Decompiling a CLI to source
text: Deobfuscates and decompiles a shipped command-line tool back into readable source code, using the same technique to convert an application into a Z80 tape.

title: USB hub firmware and protocol
text: Reverse-engineers an abandoned network USB hub's proprietary transport and firmware images, then writes a bridge that re-exports its devices over USB/IP on modern systems.

title: Yoda Stories engine decompiled
text: Decompiles a 1990s adventure game from its Ghidra project and assets, transcribing the whole engine into C++ that rebuilds an executable and is being ported to SDL.

title: PS4 rhythm game executable analysis
text: Reconstructs the startup flow, subsystem map and frame loop of a PS4 rhythm game executable from its binary, documenting each analysis milestone.

title: Smartwatch BLE protocol
text: Reverse-engineers a smartwatch's Bluetooth protocol and watch-face file format, verifying each byte against the official app's output, to install custom faces from Linux.

title: Car head unit firmware container
text: Reverse-engineers an aftermarket Android car head unit's custom firmware container byte by byte, patches binaries, and diagnoses the live device to fix its CarPlay stack.

title: Endoscope protocols decoded
text: Reverse-engineers cheap USB and Wi-Fi endoscopes, then writes and flashes Python and Arduino libraries developed with hardware in the loop.

title: Malicious cracks unpacked
text: Reverse-engineers obfuscated malicious software cracks with a Ghidra plugin, recovering their full behavior from the decompiled code.

title: SaaS backend cloned from its apps
text: Reverse-engineers a platform's open-source mobile apps and web front end to build a functionally identical, API-compatible backend, reportedly in about a week of evenings.

title: Transport-sim game functions named
text: Reverse-engineers an old transportation-sim game in Ghidra, working out what each function does and naming functions and variables to match.

title: Ransomware decryptor rebuilt
text: Reverse-engineers a ransomware encryptor and its decryptor in Ghidra to build a more reliable decryptor that recovers terabytes of locked data.

title: Keys found in a DLL
text: Walks through Ghidra to locate the initialization vector and credentials inside a DLL, then writes a Python script that decrypts the application's data.

title: Private server for a dead game
text: Builds a private server for a shut-down online game by driving Ghidra, a debugger and UI automation against its client, getting login, chat and inventory working over four days.

title: Z80 game physics mod
text: Modifies a 40-year-old Z80 game by reading its disassembly, locating unused memory, and writing assembly changes that add Super Mario-style physics.

title: NES ROM hacks without assembly skills
text: Makes small hacks to NES ROMs by disassembling them, without prior knowledge of 6502 assembly or the console's hardware.

title: Mainframe panel switches disassembled
text: Reads the switch positions of a 1960s mainframe's dead-start panel from a photo and disassembles them into annotated instructions.

title: Private framework glass icon rendering
text: Unpacks private framework class metadata from an operating system, disassembles each method, and converts the assembly into readable Objective-C to learn how glass icon rendering works.

title: Atari game unlimited lives
text: Reverse-engineers an 8-kilobyte Atari 8-bit game ROM through a Ghidra connector, renaming functions and locating the lives logic to patch in unlimited lives.

title: Bluetooth gadget protocol to Linux app
text: Reverse-engineers an Android companion app's Bluetooth traffic to a gadget and builds a Linux app for the same device in a few prompts.

title: File format and XOR payload decoded
text: Reverse-engineers an undocumented file format and a XOR-encrypted payload, then writes code to read and write the format.

title: Imaging station camera capture
text: Captures USB packets from a proprietary industrial camera on a scientific imaging station, works out the 16-bit image format, and replaces the awful vendor software with custom code.

title: Remote Desktop client bugs patched
text: Patches two long-standing bugs in a Windows remote desktop client by locating the faulty spots in megabytes of executable code, using NOPs and a stack offset change.

title: Patcher for a CLI binary
text: Dissects each new release of a closed command-line tool's executable to update a patcher that disables telemetry and strips performance-reducing language from its prompts.

title: Audio interface firmware and SSH
text: Captures a USB audio interface's firmware update traffic and HID messages, then edits the firmware tarball to inspect how updates work and enable SSH access.

title: RV Bluetooth control system
text: Decompiles a vendor app for an RV's smart control system to recover its Bluetooth protocol, then builds a replacement Android app, website and Home Assistant integration.

title: PCB design file format
text: Reverse-engineers the file format of a commercial PCB design tool to build a command-line editor that automates part selection and footprint work.

title: Bricked piano revived
text: Decompiles a piano maker's Android app to extract the hardcoded firmware encryption key, decrypts the update, and writes a Bluetooth flashing script that revives a bricked digital piano.

title: Tablet booting Debian from SD
text: Reverse-engineers a budget tablet's Rockchip hardware by rebuilding a device tree from stock firmware so Debian boots natively from an SD card, leaving Android untouched.

title: NAS LED control daemon
text: Reverse-engineers how a mini NAS drives its status LEDs and writes a daemon that sets them properly under Linux.

title: Online game client networking layer
text: Pulls the subsystems out of a classic online game's client with Ghidra and reconstructs a working networking layer toward a buildable replacement client.

title: SaaS internal APIs to tool server
text: Reverse-engineers a SaaS product's internal APIs to produce a more feature-rich tool server than the vendor's official one, which sits behind an enterprise plan.

title: Proprietary 4D database recovered
text: Reverse-engineers an ancient proprietary binary database format from the late 1990s, extracting the data and fully reconstructing the specification for complete recovery.

title: C64 strategy game reverse engineered
text: Reverse-engineers an old Commodore 64 strategy game from its binary, documenting its logic in a public repository.

title: Windows program decompiled for Linux
text: Decompiles an old Windows program to port it to Linux, then rewrites it as a new application.

title: Audiobook app patched for sync
text: Decompiles a closed-source Android audiobook player, adds server sync code, and recompiles the APK so playback progress syncs with a self-hosted library.

title: Camper van CAN bus integration
text: Decompiles a camper van's firmware, documents its CAN interfaces, and programs a microcontroller module to control power, heating, lighting and tanks.

title: Vintage ECU disassembler
text: Builds a disassembler and emulator to reverse-engineer a 1990s engine control unit's firmware, using the emulator to understand how sections of the code work.

title: Golf cart controller protocol
text: Maps a golf cart motor controller's full functionality by decompiling its .NET configuration app and capturing USB traffic, producing a portable C library and command-line tool.

title: Music player earbud remote support
text: Sweeps registers of an undocumented audio chip in a music player, diffing logs to learn how earbud remote buttons are detected, then adds that support to open-source firmware.

title: Electric motorcycle app and firmware
text: Decompiles an electric motorcycle's Android app and firmware with Ghidra and JADX connectors, bypassing authentication and signing arbitrary firmware during a security assessment.
